title: Grateful Dead Live at Kiel Auditorium on 1973-10-29
lineage: Dat (Sony D8) -> RME Hammerfall Digiface -> Sony Vaio C1VP ->
source: SBD -> Master Reel (7inch Master Reels @ 7.5ips 1/2trk) -> DCassette (Tascam 122mkIII) -> Dat (Panasonic 3700/44.1k) D

ai_review.summary: High‑energy ’73 show with stellar Eyes of the World and China Doll, captured on a crisp soundboard mix despite some audience patches.
ai_review.review: The performance is consistently praised for its soaring energy, tight interplay and standout moments like the immaculate Eyes > China Doll sequence, an incendiary Other One, and powerful renditions of Bertha, Truckin' and Brokedown Palace. The recording is a soundboard source with excellent instrument separation and a great overall mix, though a few audience‑sourced patches (especially on “El Paso”) and slight pitch drift keep it from being flawless.

ai_rating.rationale: The vast majority of reviews rate the show 4‑5 stars, highlighting exceptional musical moments and a generally high‑quality soundboard recording; only minor criticisms about audience patches keep the rating just below perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp instrument separation and solid mix praised, but several reviewers note rough audience patches (notably on El Paso) and a slight pitch inconsistency; one comment mentions Bob’s guitar being too forward in the mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Honky‑tonk first set with surprise highlights (Tennessee Jed, Mexicali Blues) leading into a high‑energy second set that builds intensity through a superb Eyes > China Doll transition and jazzy jams on Truckin' and The Other One.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers praise his unique, tuba‑like guitar tones and relentless solo work throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Credited with a booming transition into China Doll and strong jazz‑inflected playing on Truckin' and The Other One.
band_member_comments.Bob: One reviewer notes his rhythm guitar is mixed too far forward; otherwise his contributions are generally appreciated.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano work is highlighted for jazzy, McCoy‑Tyner‑style chords that drive the Truckin' outro and other improvisations.
